pages.name: The last mile of research is a separate layer, prepared in the days after acceptance, and three gaps remain open

elements.text: §1 INTRODUCTION
The last mile of research is a separate layer, prepared in the days after
acceptance, and three gaps remain open
Poster, talk video, and blog piece each need figure selection, layout, narration, or audience-appropriate writing (§1)
The dissemination layer covers the poster you stand next to at a conference session, the talk video on the venue's virtual track or the lab's channel, and
the blog piece shared through social media. Authors prepare all three in the days right after acceptance, at exactly the moment they have the least time
to spare; labs, courses, and multilingual organizations reuse the same layer.
Paper-to-poster, paper-to-video, and paper-to-blog systems, plus the multi-artifact suites PaperX and OmniPresent, shift the question from whether
several formats can be generated to
whether the artifacts remain native-editable and navigable
G1
Shared grounding
Combining artifact-specific systems repeats
figure, caption, and metadata extraction, and
leaves cross-artifact references for the user to
reconcile.
G2
Native editability
A multi-format suite does not by itself give
native-editable source files for every artifact in
the author's PowerPoint and Word workflow.
G3
Experience-level convergence
Parallel or consistently rendered outputs do not
bind poster regions, video segments, and blog
passages into one interactive surface for
revision and reuse.
WHO ELSE THE LAST MILE SERVES (§1)
The accepted-paper author
the poster, talk video, and blog piece prepared in the days after
acceptance, right after the camera-ready
An industrial research lab
public-facing communications for every accepted paper,
polished by a communications team
A course or multilingual organization
a graduate course's paper-of-the-week briefing pack;
cross-region outreach in more than one language

CONTRIBUTIONS, AS THE AUTHORS STATE THEM
The workspace itself: one paper PDF becomes a print-ready conference poster,
a narrated talk video, and a bilingual blog through composable skills.
Paper2Reel, an experience-level convergence layer whose interactions connect
poster regions, video segments, and blog passages in one navigable HTML
surface.
A delivery contract: one shared Paper2Assets bundle plus native-editable
sources — PowerPoint for the poster and the video deck, Word for the bilingual
blog.
Posters best among automated systems on all three aesthetic sub-criteria and
best or tied-best on two of three information sub-criteria; about 17.5% above the
authors' own on aesthetics (3.56 vs 3.03); overall wins on 74 and 95 of 100
papers under the two judges. The video ships narration-aligned highlights,
burned-in and sidecar subtitles, and duration control; the blog ships in two
languages with layout-aware DOCX repair.
Runtimes: Claude Code and Codex skill mechanisms; deterministic primitives — headless
Chromium (HTML→PDF), LibreOffice + ffmpeg (slides→video), python-docx (.docx); Edge TTS
for narration. The runtime itself is not a contribution.
Source: arXiv:2607.04438 v2 (19 Jul 2026)

WHAT THE BUNDLE HOLDS
Full body text with page breaks; detected figure captions; a per-figure manifest; cleaned figure images
Metadata: title, authors, institutes, venue, paper and code links; best-effort institution and venue logos; QR codes
The nine-section summary — Problem, Motivation, Contribution, Method, Dataset/Benchmark, Key Result, Ablation,
Headline Numbers, Takeaway — plus the inventory manifest, per-section records with stable ids, and the narration clip

Single-owner extraction
Downstream skills read the bundle and never re-open the PDF. A
stable figure-naming invariant means the figure the poster's method

idempotent script, so a failed stage re-runs in isolation.

pages.name: The fill loop is discrete: five verdict bands, one section edited per round, termination as a categorical fixed point

elements.text: SKILL 2 OF 5 · §2.2.2 STAGED-FILL LOOP
The fill loop is discrete: five verdict bands, one section edited per round,
termination as a categorical fixed point
fullRatio = content height ÷ card height; the verdict alone selects the move; Figure 4 shows one poster converging
EMPTY below 0.70
append a reserve paragraph or promote an optional section
SPARSE 0.70–0.90
polish up: pad prose or enlarge a widget to reach the card floor
the target band, left untouched
SPILLAGE 0.98–1.10
polish down: tighten prose until it re-enters the band
OVERFLOW above 1.10
drop a reserve paragraph or an entire optional section
WHY IT TERMINATES
Each move is sized by the signed pixel delta the measurement reports, never guessed
The loop refuses to re-apply a move that already overshot the band on a section
An on-disk round counter trips a circuit breaker (bounded ≈ 12 rounds) and ships the best-measured
state

P2P leads both Quiz splits: its portrait canvas is packed with near-verbatim prose, at some of the lowest aesthetic

The authors' caution, kept

pages.name: Three contexts span the dissemination spectrum on one pipeline: a camera-ready week, a lab's intake, a course's weekly packs

elements.text: §3 CAPABILITY COVERAGE · §4 APPLICATIONS
Three contexts span the dissemination spectrum on one pipeline: a
camera-ready week, a lab's intake, a course's weekly packs
Who runs it, which artifacts they lean on, what they revise; Tables 2–3 audit what the video and blog generators emit
§4.1 The author's last mile
ONE-OFF, SINGLE PAPER
One Claude Code session per paper: one extraction pass
populates the bundle, then the three generators emit an editable
.pptx, a synchronized video.pptx + .mp4 pair, and a bilingual
Word .docx pair the author hand-revises rather than
regenerates — all navigable through one reel.html that doubles
as a review surface for co-authors.
LEANS ON
editable .pptx poster
video.pptx + .mp4 pair
bilingual .docx pair
reel.html as a review surface
§4.2 Lab and org communication
CONTINUOUS, PER ACCEPTED PAPER
Wired into the publication-intake pipeline so every accepted
paper auto-generates draft dissemination artifacts an editorial or
communications team then polishes. The editable PowerPoint
and Word outputs make it a draft-and-revise workflow; the
bilingual blog covers a Chinese-WeChat and an English
research-blog register from one evidence map.
LEANS ON
draft artifacts per accepted paper
PowerPoint and Word for hand-off
one reel per paper for the comms team
§4.3 Educational reuse
PERIODIC, MANY-PAPER BATCH
A course, reading group, or public-understanding outlet feeds a
reading list through the pipeline to produce paper-of-the-week
briefing packs: a lecture deck, an asynchronous talk video, a
newsletter blog. Instructors adjust framing or drop a slide;
re-running on a corrected PDF re-issues the whole pack.
LEANS ON
lecture deck
asynchronous talk video
newsletter blog
versioned bundle per paper
CAPABILITY AUDITS, TABLES 2 AND 3
Table 2 (video) asks whether a system emits visual attention cues or cursor grounding, an editable
PPTX deck, duration control, and narration audio; Table 3 (blog) asks about layout checks, embedded
figures, editable DOCX output, and paper-input summarization.
The audited products and research systems generally cover a single artifact; ResearchStudio-Reel
emits all three, exposes the shared bundle, includes a native-editable source in each package, and
stitches them into one surface. The audit documents breadth of the contract; it does not measure editing
effort or the viewer's usability.
GAP TO HUMAN POSTERS
Matching or exceeding the aggregate judge scores does not mean the output is on par with an author's own
poster. A human designer routinely adds material the paper does not contain — a purpose-drawn method or
overview diagram, explanatory icons — whereas the pipeline is grounded in the extracted bundle and reuses
only figures and content that appear in the paper. Author taste also spans a wide, legitimate range; the pipeline
analyses each paper's figure and content profile and chooses the layout that fits it, aiming for a sensible middle
ground rather than any single house style.
Source: arXiv:2607.04438 v2 (19 Jul 2026)

pages.name: Five failure modes recur in end-to-end runs; the system is calibrated on ML / CV / NLP venues only; quantitative evaluation covers the poster

elements.text: APPENDIX A · LIMITATIONS
Five failure modes recur in end-to-end runs; the system is calibrated on ML / CV /
NLP venues only; quantitative evaluation covers the poster
Each failure mode has a named mitigation; video and blog are compared on capability only; no human-rater study exists yet
DOMAIN SCOPE
Calibrated on ML, CV, and NLP venues, where paper layout, figure
conventions, and the claim–evidence structure are relatively uniform.
Transfer to biomedicine, physics, or design-heavy fields is untested and
each skill's move catalogue may need extending; the primitives are
domain-agnostic, but each venue family should be validated end-to-end
before deployment.
EVALUATION COVERAGE
Quantitative results are reported only for the poster, under two VLM
judges on the Paper2Poster benchmark; the video benchmark of
Paper2Video [4] is not applied. The audits in Tables 2–3 document
output contracts but do not measure human editing effort, fidelity after
edits, or whether section-level navigation improves understanding. RRP
(§2.2) is an in-loop signal, not a headline metric; a third-party
human-rater study across all three artifacts is left for future work.
Appendix B, provenance and disclosure
A narrated video with burned-in subtitles is not obviously AI-produced at a glance. The authors recommend that deployments preserve
provenance metadata — which skill and version, which bundle checksum, which theme, header, or TTS voice, which model — so readers
can audit the generation chain and, where required, disclose AI involvement; the inventory manifest and the video QA record already carry
this ancestry.
LICENSING, APPENDIX B
Per-figure copyright on extracted figures follows the source paper's
license; logos follow Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata; the edge-tts
client accesses Microsoft Edge's online service, so deployments verify
the service terms. The pipeline redistributes neither figures nor logos:
the user runs it on their own paper.
Source: arXiv:2607.04438 v2 (19 Jul 2026)

pages.name: Supported: a native-editable, section-aligned workspace with testable gates. Open: reading-and-recall evaluation and bespoke diagrams

elements.text: §6 FUTURE WORK · §7 CONCLUSION
Supported: a native-editable, section-aligned workspace with testable gates.
Open: reading-and-recall evaluation and bespoke diagrams
From one-way automation to a workflow authors can inspect, navigate, and revise; the paper names the limits of its own proxies
ESTABLISHED BY THE PAPER
Five composable skills, one bundle, three native-editable artifacts
One Paper2Assets bundle feeds a native-editable PowerPoint poster and video deck and a
bilingual Word blog; Paper2Reel binds their sections, slides, video times, captions, and
passages.
Posters judged above the authors' own on aesthetics
Best among automated systems on all three aesthetic sub-criteria and best or tied-best on two
of three information sub-criteria under two VLM judges; 3.56 vs 3.03; overall wins on 74 and 95
of 100 papers.
A pattern that may travel
The delivery-contract pattern may extend to other targets with native authoring formats,
deterministic renderers, and testable package criteria — with its evaluative, generative, and
architectural limits still to be studied (§6).
TWO GAPS THAT MATTER MORE THAN COVERAGE
Evaluation is proxy-bound
The aesthetic rubric and PaperQuiz pull in opposite directions — a denser poster
wins comprehension while a cleaner one wins aesthetics — and neither
measures whether a reader absorbs the work. The measured-fill loop optimizes a
geometric density target, not understanding; the honest next step is to close the
loop on a controlled human reading-and-recall signal rather than on a proxy a
denser poster can always game.
The generative gap
Because the pipeline reuses only figures that already exist in the paper, it cannot
yet produce the bespoke method or overview diagrams human designers add to
carry the narrative. Addressing this may require faithful figure synthesis, which
reintroduces the hallucination risk the categorical gates were built to suppress,
and would push gate discipline from layout onto the factual content of generated
visuals.
THE PAPER'S CLOSING SENTENCE, §7
“By keeping generated artifacts editable and connected after generation, ResearchStudio-Reel shifts the last mile from one-way automation toward a workflow authors
can inspect, navigate, and revise.”
Source: arXiv:2607.04438 v2 (19 Jul 2026)
